content.title: Submit a valid manuscript to an available publishing package and receive confirmation and reduced seat availability
content.intent: Prove that a complete valid submission succeeds, returns the authored confirmation details and reference, and reduces the package's shared remaining seat count by one.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: Equivalence partitioning for a valid complete field set; CRUD round-trip for the persisted submission write; State / flow for submit-and-return behavior. Risk judged high because money and shared-capacity rules apply, so this write path was retained first under max_pairs=3.

content.title: Submit a manuscript with a stale or unoffered onboarding seat and receive the seat-unavailable rejection
content.intent: Prove that a seat value that is no longer available or was never offered is rejected with the seat-unavailable message and no successful submission.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: Negative / error for rejected submission; Equivalence partitioning across two invalid seat classes that share one expected outcome. Risk judged high because a stale or forged seat can overbook shared monthly capacity on a priced package, so this path was retained under max_pairs=3.

content.title: Open a fully booked publishing package detail page and see the booked message instead of a submission form
content.intent: Prove that a package with no seats left suppresses the submission form and shows the fully booked message on its detail page.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: Boundary value analysis on the zero-seats-left boundary; Negative / error because the user must be blocked from starting a submission; Persistence of the shared-capacity state in the rendered package detail page. Risk judged high because this terminal capacity state prevents futile submissions and misleading availability claims.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value: this is the revenue-bearing primary path and the only path that proves submission creation, authored confirmation content, and the shared seat-count decrement after a write.
[value_score] Very high value: it protects the shared monthly-capacity rule against stale or forged seat values, which would otherwise oversubscribe a priced package.
[value_score] High value: it proves the terminal capacity boundary where the form must be suppressed entirely, preventing futile or misleading submission attempts.
[value_score] Useful but lower than capacity rules under the budget: required-field validation is explicit and important, but it does not protect shared inventory or the successful paid-intent path.
[value_score] Useful but lowest under the budget: manuscript-status validation is a single-field negative distinct from the more consequential inventory and success paths.

[applicability] Applied happy-path, equivalence-partition, CRUD, and state-flow techniques because the use case creates a persisted submission and returns to the package page with a changed shared-capacity state.
[applicability] Applied negative and equivalence-partition techniques because two invalid seat classes share one rejection outcome and both threaten the same capacity rule.
[applicability] Applied boundary and negative techniques because zero remaining seats is the explicit terminal limit where the submission surface must be suppressed.
[applicability] Applied negative and equivalence-partition techniques because each missing required field should lead to the same rejection and no-creation outcome; budget later evicted it.
[applicability] Applied negative technique because leaving manuscript status at its default prompt should block submission with a distinct error message; budget later evicted it.
